rules: Do not delete, move, truncate, overwrite, reset, clean, prune, garbage-collect, archive, or deaccession any project-related file or directory before content-level reconciliation.
Folder names such as archive, backup, worktree, generated, library, cache, old, duplicate, consolidated, temp, build, or node_modules are not sufficient grounds for deletion.

Before any future disposition: inspect contents, hash exact duplicates, compare branches/commits, detect uncommitted changes, recover unique code/features/concepts/data/assets, map provenance, and record evidence.
A source may contain a more complete project than the current repository and must be treated as potentially authoritative until disproven.
Cleanup during discovery is classification-only. Physical deletion requires a later explicit evidence-backed disposition gate.
Git gc/prune/clean/reset and filesystem recursive deletion are prohibited during discovery/reconciliation phases.
priorActionDisclosure: Before this policy change, six historical/worktree node_modules trees were removed after package.json/package-lock verification; no authored source file was intentionally deleted. No further deletion is permitted under this policy.
